title: Insurance planning
objectives: Distinguish pure protection from investment-linked insurance.
body_md:
Insurance protects the plan from shocks. Check it **before** investing.

## Life cover

- **Term insurance** is pure protection and the most cost-efficient for income replacement.
- **Human life value (HLV)** method: present value of future income that the family depends on. A common shortcut is 10 to 15 times annual income, adjusted for debts and goals.
- **Endowment, money-back, ULIP** mix insurance with investment; costs are higher. Treat the two needs separately.

## Health cover

| Item | Note |
|---|---|
| Base policy + **super top-up** | Cost-efficient way to raise cover |
| **Waiting periods** | For pre-existing diseases and some treatments |
| **Co-pay, sub-limits, room rent caps** | Check before buying |
| **Portability** | Move insurers without losing credits |

## Others

Personal accident, critical illness, home and motor cover as relevant.

> **Exam tip:** Insure first with term and health; invest separately.
example: A 35-year-old earns ₹12 lakh and has a ₹40 lakh home loan. Cover of about 12 times income plus the loan, minus existing assets, is a starting point.
say: Keep insurance and investment separate; term cover is the cheapest protection.
Check waiting periods and sub-limits in the health policy.
never: Buy an endowment plan, it is both insurance and investment.
Health cover from your employer is enough forever.
